rv.q: Theater review by Raven SnookLibby Carr's achingly humane Calf Scramble is set in a sweltering barn where the cattle aren’t the only ones feeling penned in. Five teenage girls in Huntsville, Texas, are competing to win prize money by raising calves for their Future Farmers of America projects in 2007.
It's a fascinating glimpse into a particular domain, one in which faith in God, family, and hard work shapes a worldview.

cn.t: Critics praise this achingly humane look at Texas FFA teens raising calves as a fascinating glimpse into a faith-driven world, though the show earns modest scores suggesting some reservations about its execution.

vr.q: Despite a relatively slow start, the play has lovely character development and covers a lot of ground in just 90 minutes.
